questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The hard palate contains ________

options.text: Keratinised epithelium, submucosa, minor salivary glands
Keratinised epithelium, absent submucosa, no salivary glands
Non-keratinised epithelium, submucosa, minor salivary glands
Non-keratinised epithelium, absent submucosa, minor salivary glands

questions.correctAnswerText: Keratinised epithelium, submucosa, minor salivary glands
questions.explanation: The hard palate contains keratinised stratified squamous epithelium, has a submucosa, and contains minor salivary glands. This keratinised stratified squamous epithelium has regional variations and may be orthokeratinised or parakeratinised (found in hard palate and gingiva). The bony structure of the hard palate is covered by a firmly attached mucosa in the central part. In the lateral parts, the hard palate also has a submucosal layer containing blood vessels. There are minor mucous-type salivary glands in the submucosa in the posterior part of the hard palate. Note: in orthokeratinized epithelium the cell nuclei disappear in the keratinized layer, whereas in parakeratinized epithelium flattened, highly condensed nuclei remain in the cell cytoplasm of the keratinized layer until exfoliation.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The muscularis externa layer of the gut wall has ________

options.text: Inner longitudinal and outer circular muscle fibres
Inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle fibres

questions.correctAnswerText: Inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle fibres
questions.explanation: The muscularis externa has inner circular muscle fibres and outer longitudinal muscle fibres. The gut wall receives its strength mainly from the muscularis externa, which is the thick layer of muscle surrounding the submucosa and is responsible for gut movements such as peristalsis. Notes: muscularis externa contains smooth muscle except in the upper part of the esophagus, where it has only striated muscle fibres. The stomach has three layers in the muscularis externa, with an extra oblique layer. In the colon, the outer longitudinal fibres join to form prominent bundles called the taenia coli. The source includes a labelled histological section of duodenum showing the inner and outer layers of muscularis externa.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with suspected oesophageal carcinoma is planned for an endoscopic biopsy. A section of the lesion was taken and sent for histopathological examination. Which of the following layers of the gastrointestinal tract is not expected to be seen on microscopic examination of the section?
questions.explanation: The serosa is absent in the esophagus and hence is not expected to be seen on microscopic examination. The esophagus has an adventitia made up of dense fibrous tissue covering the muscularis externa. Only the lower intra-abdominal part of the esophagus has a layer of peritoneal covering over it. The source additionally illustrates the general layers of the gut tube: mucosa (lining epithelium, lamina propria and muscularis mucosae), submucosa, muscularis externa (inner circular and outer longitudinal fibres), and the outer covering.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the esophagus is false?

options.text: It is lined by stratified squamous epithelium
The upper third contains only skeletal muscle
The middle third contains both skeletal and smooth muscles
The lower third contains only skeletal muscle

questions.correctAnswerText: The lower third contains only skeletal muscle
questions.explanation: The false statement is that the lower third of the esophagus contains only skeletal muscle. The lower third consists only of smooth muscle. The esophagus consists of mucosa with non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, lamina propria and muscularis mucosae; submucosa containing compound tubuloalveolar mucous glands; muscularis externa with the usual circular and longitudinal layers; upper one-third containing only skeletal muscle fibres; middle one-third containing both skeletal and smooth muscle fibres; lower one-third containing only smooth muscle fibres; and an adventitia composed of dense fibrous tissue. Only a short length of the lower esophagus has a peritoneal covering (serosa).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Within which part of the gastric gland are the chief cells located?
questions.explanation: Chief cells are located mostly in the basal part of the gastric glands. Gastric glands are simple or branched tubular glands that lie perpendicular to the gastric mucosa. They can be identified in three main regions: basal/deep part, neck, and isthmus (which connects to the gastric pit). Chief cells, also called peptic or zymogen cells, are mostly found in the basal or deep portion of the gastric glands; they are cuboidal or low columnar, basophilic, contain prominent secretory granules, and secrete pepsinogen and lipase. Oxyntic/parietal cells are found in the upper part of the gland, are large and eosinophilic, and produce hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor. Mucous neck cells are prominent at the neck and secrete mucus. Neuroendocrine cells lie mostly in the basal/deeper parts of glands and include G cells (gastrin), D cells (somatostatin), enterochromaffin cells (serotonin), ECL cells (histamine) and P/D1 cells (ghrelin). Stem cells are undifferentiated cells that multiply and replace other cells.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the gastric glands is false?

options.text: Pyloric antrum has many acid secreting cells
Cardiac region has many mucus secreting cells

questions.correctAnswerText: Pyloric antrum has many acid secreting cells
questions.explanation: The pylorus consists mainly of mucus-secreting glands, so the statement that the pyloric antrum has many acid-secreting cells is false. Gastric glands are divided into principal/fundic glands in the body and fundus, cardiac gastric glands near the cardiac orifice, and pyloric gastric glands in the pyloric antrum. Principal glands contain chief cells, parietal cells, mucous neck cells, neuroendocrine cells and stem cells. Cardiac gastric glands are predominantly mucus secreting, though some parietal and chief cells are sparsely present. Pyloric glands predominantly contain mucus-secreting cells, along with neuroendocrine cells, especially gastrin-secreting G cells; parietal and chief cells are scarce.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The Brunner's glands are seen in _____
questions.explanation: Brunner's glands (duodenal glands) are compound tubular submucosal glands present in the upper duodenum, above the sphincter of Oddi. The alveoli are lined mostly by mucus-secreting columnar cells. Their ducts pass through the muscularis mucosae and empty into the intestinal crypts of Lieberkühn. The duodenum can be differentiated from jejunum and ileum by these submucosal glands; jejunum and ileum do not have glands in their submucosa. The source shows a histological section of normal duodenum with Brunner's glands at the submucosal layer.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: An intern accidentally sent an incompletely labelled sample of the resected bowel wall from a patient with intestinal obstruction for histopathological examination. Given below is the microscopic image of the section of the sample. Which part of the gastrointestinal tract is being visualised here?
questions.explanation: The image is a section through the ileum, evident from thin and slender villi and an aggregated lymphatic follicle (Peyer's patch) in the submucosa. These aggregations of lymphatic follicles are known as mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT), and also as gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT). Peyer's patches are found in large size and numerously in the terminal ileum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements is false about Paneth cells?

options.text: They are rich in rough endoplasmic reticulum

questions.explanation: The foamy or frothy cytoplasmic appearance is not a feature of Paneth cells; it is a feature of Goblet cells. Mucus-secreting Goblet cells contain lipid or mucinous material with a foamy appearance. Paneth cells (enzyme cells) are present only in the deeper portions of the intestinal crypts. They contain many eosinophilic secretory granules, a significant amount of rough endoplasmic reticulum, and are rich in zinc. Their products include lysozyme, which kills bacteria, and other enzymes.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 42-year-old man presented to the clinic with a history of anemia, non-bloody diarrhoea and poor appetite. A diagnosis of celiac disease is suspected and a duodenal biopsy is taken for histopathological examination. Which of the following cells are not likely to be seen on microscopic examination of the section?
questions.explanation: Neck cells are not likely to be seen on microscopy because they are not present in the small intestine. Neck cells are mucus-secreting cells present in the upper end or neck of the main gastric glands of the stomach. Stem cells are undifferentiated cells present in the wall of intestinal crypts. Goblet cells are mucus-secreting cells with an expanded upper part distended with mucin granules and a flattened basal nucleus. Paneth (zymogen) cells are found only in the deeper parts of intestinal crypts and contain prominent eosinophilic secretory granules.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: In which of the following structures are centroacinar cells mainly present?
questions.explanation: Centroacinar cells are mainly present in the pancreas. They are present in the alveoli of the exocrine pancreas and are so named because they are visible near the centre of the acinus (or alveolus). These cells are actually part of the intercalated ducts that are invaginated into the secretory elements of the pancreas.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following structures does not form the portal triad of the liver?
questions.explanation: Hepatic vein does not form part of the portal triad. Portal canals are present at angular intervals at the periphery of each hepatic lobule and contain connective tissue. Each portal canal contains a branch of the portal vein, a branch of the hepatic artery and an interlobular bile duct; these three structures collectively form the portal triad. The source includes a cross-section of normal hepatic tissue illustrating the portal triad.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The space of Disse consists of all of the following except ______
questions.explanation: The space of Disse contains the listed components except Kupffer cells. Kupffer cells, also called stellate macrophages or Kupffer-Browicz cells, are specialized macrophages present in the liver and are part of the mononuclear phagocyte system; they lie in the lining of the sinusoidal walls rather than in the space of Disse. The space of Disse, or perisinusoidal space, is between the hepatocyte and a sinusoid. It contains blood plasma. Microvilli of hepatocytes extend into the space, allowing absorption of proteins and other plasma components from sinusoids by hepatocytes. This space may also have some fat cells.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The transitional epithelium lines all of the following except _____
questions.explanation: Transitional epithelium lines all the listed structures except the membranous urethra. Transitional epithelium is found in the renal pelvis and calyces, ureter, urinary bladder, and pre-prostatic and prostatic parts of the urethra; because of this distribution, it is also called urothelium. Much of the urethra in both sexes is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium. The pre-prostatic and prostatic urethra have transitional epithelium, the membranous urethra is pseudostratified/stratified columnar, and the penile/spongy urethra is proximally pseudostratified columnar and distally stratified squamous.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: In which of the following structures is the type of epithelium as shown in the image seen?
questions.explanation: The image shows transitional epithelium and is seen in the urinary bladder. The deepest layer has columnar cells, the middle layers are polyhedral, and the surface layer has large, characteristic umbrella cells. Transitional epithelium is found in the renal pelvis and calyces, ureter, urinary bladder and part of the urethra, hence the term urothelium. In the urinary bladder it can stretch considerably without being damaged; when stretched, it appears thinner and the cells become flattened or rounded.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following are the epithelial supporting cells of the seminiferous tubules?
questions.explanation: Sertoli cells, also called sustentacular cells, are the epithelial supporting cells of the seminiferous tubules. They are derived from the epithelial sex cords of the developing gonads. They are tall simple columnar cells that surround proliferating and differentiating germ cells, forming pockets around them. Sertoli cells provide nutrients and phagocytose excess cytoplasm from newly forming spermatozoa. The source includes a section of seminiferous ducts illustrating the different cell types.

questions.explanation: Among the given options the histological section is most likely vas deferens or ductus deferens. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Identify the structure shown in the image below.
questions.explanation: Among the given options, the histological image is most likely endometrium. It shows glycogen masses in the basal cytoplasm of epithelial cells lining glands, a feature of the early secretory phase of the endometrium. The uterus has an outer smooth-muscle myometrium and an inner endometrium. The endometrium has three layers: stratum compactum, stratum spongiosum (together forming the stratum functionalis), and stratum basalis. During the menstrual cycle the endometrium progressively thickens, uterine glands grow in length and become tortuous/saw-toothed during the secretory phase, and glandular epithelium changes from cuboidal to columnar with glycogen vacuoles.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The structures marked in the image below are found in the epithelial lining of all of the following sites, except:
questions.explanation: The arrow marks cilia. All the structures listed in the options have ciliated lining epithelium except the epididymis, which is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia. The source image is a histological section of epididymis showing pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia. Cilia are minute hair-like projections, while stereocilia are very long, thick microvilli. Ciliated columnar epithelium occurs in much of the respiratory tract, uterus and uterine tube, efferent ductules of the testis, parts of the middle ear and auditory tube, ependymal lining, central canal of the spinal cord and ventricles of the brain. Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium is seen in the trachea and large bronchi.
